chunks: Tell: O People of the Book, do not overstep the bounds in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who had erred before, and led many astray, and wandered from the right path.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran command the People of the Book to avoid in their religion?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a direct address to the People of the Book, particularly Christians, warning against the exaggeration of divine attributes (ghuluw) and adherence to subjective desires (ahwa') that led to their deviation. It underscores the necessity of returning to the 'straight path' (sawā' al-sabīl) through adherence to divine revelation and the Imams, who are seen as the guardians of the true path. The verse serves as a foundational critique of theological innovation and a call to monotheistic purity.
